lines.text: How long does a bullet take?
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ lˈɔŋ dˈʌz ɐ bˈʊlɪt tˈeɪk?

lines.text: A famous old photograph by Harold Edgerton shows a bullet going through an apple. That bullet flew at about eight hundred fifty meters a second. The apple is about eight centimeters across. So the bullet crosses it in less than a ten-thousandth of a second. Here, that takes about one second. The bullet is a small, dark shape. At this speed, you can watch it drift into the apple like a slow fish. The skin dimples.
lines.phonemes: ɐ fˈeɪməs ˈoʊld fˈoʊɾəɡɹˌæf baɪ hˈæɹəld ˈɛdʒətən ʃˈoʊz ɐ bˈʊlɪt ɡˌoʊɪŋ θɹuː ɐn ˈæpəl. ðæt bˈʊlɪt flˈuː æɾ ɐbˌaʊt ˈeɪt hˈʌndɹɪd fˈɪfti mˈiːɾɚz ɐ sˈɛkənd. ðɪ ˈæpəl ɪz ɐbˌaʊt ˈeɪt sˈɛntɪmˌiːɾɚz əkɹˈɑːs. sˌoʊ ðə bˈʊlɪt kɹˈɔsᵻz ɪɾ ɪn lˈɛs ðˌænə tˈɛnθˈaʊzəndθ əvə sˈɛkənd. hˈɪɹ, ðæt tˈeɪks ɐbˌaʊt wˈʌn sˈɛkənd. ðə bˈʊlɪt ɪz ɐ smˈɔːl, dˈɑːɹk ʃˈeɪp. æt ðɪs spˈiːd, juː kæn wˈɑːtʃ ɪt dɹˈɪft ˌɪntʊ ðɪ ˈæpəl lˈaɪk ɐ slˈoʊ fˈɪʃ. ðə skˈɪn dˈɪmpəlz.

lines.text: Then the back of the apple blows outward, in a spray. And the bullet is already past. In real time, that was far too quick to blink. It's moving more than twice as fast as sound, so it drags a narrow cone of air behind it. Quick pause: if that one got you, tap like and follow. Okay, back to it. A bullet is fast. But out the window, something is about to be much faster.
lines.phonemes: ðˈɛn ðə bˈæk ʌvðɪ ˈæpəl blˈoʊz ˈaʊtwɚd, ɪn ɐ spɹˈeɪ. ænd ðə bˈʊlɪt ɪz ɔːlɹˌɛdi pˈæst. ɪn ɹˈiːəl tˈaɪm, ðæt wʌz fˈɑːɹ tˈuː kwˈɪk tə blˈɪŋk. ɪts mˈuːvɪŋ mˈɔːɹ ðɐn twˈaɪs æz fˈæst æz sˈaʊnd, sˌoʊ ɪt dɹˈæɡz ɐ nˈæɹoʊ kˈoʊn ʌv ˈɛɹ bᵻhˈaɪnd ɪt. kwˈɪk pˈɔːz: ɪf ðˈætwˌʌn ɡˈɑːt juː, tˈæp lˈaɪk ænd fˈɑːloʊ. oʊkˈeɪ, bˈæk tʊ ɪt. ɐ bˈʊlɪt ɪz fˈæst. bˌʌt ˈaʊt ðə wˈɪndoʊ, sˈʌmθɪŋ ɪz ɐbˌaʊt təbi mˈʌtʃ fˈæstɚ.
